title: Bessie Coleman: Queen of the Air
passage: Bessie Coleman was born in 1892 in a small town in Texas. Growing up in a world where opportunities were limited for African Americans and women, Bessie dreamed of a bigger life. While working as a manicurist in Chicago, she heard stories from pilots returning from World War I. These stories ignited a passion in her: she wanted to fly. However, no flight school in the United States would admit her because of her race and gender. Instead of giving up, Bessie learned French and moved to France in 1920. There, she earned her international pilot's license in just seven months, becoming the first African American woman to do so. When she returned to the U.S., she became a famous stunt pilot known as 'Queen Bess.' She used her fame to encourage other African Americans to fly and refused to perform at any airshows that didn't allow everyone to use the same entrance, standing up for equality until the very end.
